clue.text: Chicken served with the French seafood

le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: A restaurant dish of chicken with the French-style seafood on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chicken served with' reads as a menu; 'served with' only joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockle is an edible bivalve shellfish, so it is an example of seafood.

clue.text: Provider of victuals to pet visiting two queens

blocks.note: a cat is a household pet

explanation.surface: Someone supplying food for a pet staying with royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the standard crossword queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterer supplies food and drink for events, so is a provider of victuals, an old word for food.

clue.text: Dog found by conscientious objector and Republican soldier

blocks.note: CO is the abbreviation for conscientious objector
R is the abbreviation for Republican
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A dog discovered by a pacifist and a Republican soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: The corgi is a small short-legged Welsh breed of dog, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Convict caught while being served with northeast Italian food

explanation.surface: A prisoner seized while being served a dish from the northeast of Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'northeast Italian' looks like a region; NE is a separate piece and the definition is just 'Italian food'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagne is a baked Italian dish of flat pasta sheets layered with sauce and cheese.

clue.text: Drug legal to bring out

blocks.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Talk of making a drug legal so that it can be brought out onto the market.
explanation.walkthrough: E for ecstasy is a standard crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To elicit a response or fact is to draw it out of someone, a direct synonym of bring out.

clue.text: Generosity of regal runaway on ship

SS is steamship

explanation.definitionFit: Largess is generous giving of gifts or money, a noun for generosity.

clue.text: Work together in confined space with energy and speed

blocks.note: a coop is a small cramped pen, as for hens
E is the physics symbol for energy
rate means speed

explanation.surface: Instructions to collaborate quickly and energetically in a cramped room.
explanation.definitionFit: To cooperate is to act jointly with others towards a shared aim, which is working together.

clue.text: Plays performed here and broadcast at three

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Plays are staged and also aired on radio at three o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' suggests radio drama, but it means scattered.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre is the building where plays are staged before an audience.

clue.text: Proust disconcerted by vegetable

indicators.note: disconcerted means thrown into disorder, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the French novelist's name taken as written

explanation.surface: The French novelist Marcel Proust unsettled by a vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: A sprout is short for Brussels sprout, a small green cabbage-like vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprout, the Brussels sprout, is a green vegetable, an example of the class.

clue.text: Crap spouses sort out not communicating effectively

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Useless husbands and wives should resolve their failure to talk to each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort out' reads as a phrasal verb meaning resolve, but 'sort' is fodder and only 'out' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: People at cross purposes misunderstand each other, each talking about something different, so communication fails.

clue.text: Headless fish going astray

indicators.note: without a head means the opening letter of the word is cut off

blocks.note: a herring is a common sea fish

explanation.surface: A decapitated fish wandering off course, an absurd picture.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the H from HERRING leaves ERRING.
explanation.definitionFit: To err is to stray from the right path, so erring is a present participle meaning going astray.

clue.text: Some let teenagers consume egg dish

blocks.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.walkthrough: The answer starts after the S of 'Some' and ends just inside 'teenagers'.
explanation.definitionFit: An omelette is beaten eggs cooked in a pan, a classic egg-based dish.

clue.text: Row of houses by moonlight?

blocks.note: surface reading: a terrace of houses seen at night
setter's reading: the curved row takes the name of a moon shape seen in its thinner phases

explanation.surface: A street of terraced houses lit by the moon.
explanation.walkthrough: A curved row of houses is called by the same word as the sliver shape of the moon, which the question mark hints at.
explanation.definitionFit: In British towns a crescent is a street of houses built in a curve, named after the curved lunar shape.

clue.text: I seem most upset now and then

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are reshuffled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone admitting they appear most distressed only occasionally.
explanation.definitionFit: Sometimes and now and then are adverbs meaning occasionally, on some occasions but not all.

clue.text: "Pieces of meat", said Poles

blocks.note: steaks are thick slices of meat

explanation.surface: Someone from Poland announcing 'pieces of meat' at a butcher's.
explanation.walkthrough: Poles looks like the people of Poland; it is the definition, wooden posts.
explanation.definitionFit: Stakes are pointed wooden posts driven into the ground, which are poles.

clue.text: Before end of innings, heartless Somerset umpire dismisses batsman

indicators.note: without its heart a word keeps only its outside letters
the end of a word is its final letter alone

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the county name
ump is a short form of umpire
the final letter of innings

explanation.surface: A cricket scene: a cruel Somerset umpire gives a batsman out just before the innings ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' places the earlier pieces ahead of the last letter of innings. Somerset is an English county with a cricket team.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the wicketkeeper stumps a batsman by breaking the wicket while he is out of his ground, getting him out.

clue.text: Lose one's footing on oil spilt in Libyan city

blocks.note: to trip is to stumble
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone slips on spilled oil in a city in Libya.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripoli is the capital of Libya, so it is a Libyan city.

clue.text: Struck with a heavy blow by end of Lewis's glove

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter alone

blocks.note: the final letter of Lewis's
a mitten is a glove without separate fingers

explanation.surface: Hit hard by a boxer's glove, perhaps Lennox Lewis's.
explanation.walkthrough: Lennox Lewis was a British heavyweight boxing champion, which makes the glove a boxing glove in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Smitten is the past participle of smite, an old verb meaning to hit hard.

clue.text: Author and editor kept busy with trifling tasks

blocks.note: Beatrix Potter, the children's author

explanation.surface: A writer and their editor filling time with small jobs.

explanation.definitionFit: To potter is to occupy oneself in a relaxed way with small unimportant jobs, so the past tense fits.

clue.text: Priest meeting one and all to give religious instruction

blocks.note: Pr is the abbreviation for priest
each covers every one in a group

explanation.surface: A clergyman meets everyone to teach them about faith.
explanation.definitionFit: To preach is to deliver a sermon, which is giving religious instruction.

clue.text: On reflection, not guaranteed to get a haircut

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things back to front

blocks.note: taken as written, then turned round
sure means certain or guaranteed

explanation.surface: Thinking it over, a haircut is not certain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On reflection' reads as 'after thought' but turns round the word that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonsure is the shaved crown of a monk's head, a particular kind of haircut.

clue.text: Body part delivered by a murder suspect

indicators.note: suspect means dubious or not sound, so the letters are not to be trusted in their order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Human remains left behind by someone suspected of killing.
explanation.definitionFit: The eardrum is the membrane in the ear that vibrates with sound, a part of the body.

clue.text: Dreadful class of people reported for abusive speech

indicators.note: a report is spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: dire means dreadful; in non-rhotic British speech it sounds like these three letters
a tribe is a social group of people

explanation.surface: A terrible social group being reported for hate speech.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'Dreadful' is taken by its sound; British speakers drop the final R, so 'dire' and the opening of the answer sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter verbal attack, a forceful and abusive piece of speech or writing.

clue.text: No sailor close to mutiny gets someone to prepare legal documents

blocks.note: taken as written
tar is an old word for a sailor
the final letter of mutiny

explanation.definitionFit: A notary is an official authorised to draw up and certify legal documents such as deeds and contracts.

clue.text: Drunk and reluctant to stand a round

second meaning: stingy with money, unwilling to buy drinks for others

explanation.surface: A tipsy pub-goer who never buys the drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: To stand a round is to buy drinks for everyone in your group at the pub.

clue.text: Gruesome tics cry out for procedure to make face more appealing

definitions.text: procedure to make face more appealing

indicators.note: letters put out of order are no longer in their written sequence, so they are rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: 'cry out for' reads as a single phrase meaning demand, but 'cry' is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmetic surgery is an operation done to improve appearance, such as a facelift, rather than for health.

clue.text: Maintains anecdote's crazy

blocks.note: the letters straddle the two words

clue.text: Treatment for psychosis in strange part of the body!

explanation.surface: An exclamation at finding psychiatric treatment in an odd part of the body.
